title: Extended color palette
slide_intent: Explain how signature colors expand into a working palette because compositions need supporting tones as well as distinctive brand hues.
strategic_value: Neutral bases and a wider hue range can support varied content while retaining orange as a recognizable emphasis.
demonstration: A rectangular matrix places broad dark-neutral, light-neutral and orange columns beside narrow red, yellow, green and turquoise scales.
practical_value: Compare the hierarchy of palette families; do not infer numeric color values or required area ratios.

content_islands.name: Neutral scales
content_islands.spec: Keep broad dark and light neutral columns on the left.

content_islands.name: Chromatic scales
content_islands.spec: Place the broad orange column beside narrower chromatic columns; retain the horizontal tint and shade bands.

reference_purposes.Expression: The matrix displays neutral and chromatic families across multiple lightness values.
reference_purposes.Intent: Pentagram explains that warm gray bases provide neutrality and that orange forms the midpoint between logo red and yellow.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The accompanying article explicitly specifies warm grays as the base for compositions and orange as the new primary color.

ingredient.name: Extended palette
ingredient.role: Support varied communication around a distinctive orange emphasis.
ingredient.application: Use warm grays as composition bases and orange as primary color, as specified in the accompanying article.
ingredient.scope: Historical 2016 Pentagram case study; not a current master guideline or numeric production specification.
